Mir, morning routine

pedūlia, pedūlium n. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

Socks in modern spoken Latin; Mir’s transcribed routine uses the word in this sense. The classical adjective is pedūlis, pedūle, “for the feet.”

Other words

  • impilia, impilium n. pl. — felt foot-coverings

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Plin. NH 19.32 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 382

    Another modern choice for socks.

  • ūdō, ūdōnis m. — felt or fur sock

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Mart. 14.140 (Lewis & Short)

    Ancient, and historically more specific. Plural ūdōnēs.

  • fasciae pedūlēs — foot-wraps

    also used · post-classical · Dig. 34.2.26 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • Pedūlia indue.

    Put your socks on.composed

  • Pedūlia exue.

    Take your socks off.composed

See also stockings, shoe, T-shirt, tights.
